rationale: All four round-1 findings (CR-001..CR-004) are resolved by commit dd10ef920 (7 files, +139/-4), the 216-line fix-up diff introduces no new high-risk issue so no confirmation pass was needed, lint/license are clean and 848 tests in the affected scope pass. The business_review rows carried forward still show the partials that these four findings caused. Round 1's coverage note stands: its test-diff coverage was limited to the acceptance lens.

standards_review.notes: 5 commits, all 'EPMCDME-15558: <description>' with the required attribution lines
make ruff clean, make license-check clean (2453 files); layering respected (tool -> service -> repository); tests mirror src

Download rule D2 and path validation reviewed: no authorization hole. Reserved-path fold order raised as CR-003. Residual (deferred): a stale workspace reference keeps a skill blob downloadable after the skill is unshared

finding_status.notes: skill_workspace_seeder._seed_one now logs a warning with the skill, the folder, the count and per-reason counts whenever the plan skipped anything, including the all-skipped legacy case; three tests cover over-limit plus inline, repeat logging for a legacy skill, and silence when nothing is skipped
plan_bundle_seed iterates sorted(files, key=path); test_files_are_planned_in_path_order_whatever_the_stored_order asserts a, b are seeded and c is skipped at a limit of 2

is_reserved_path folds (NFKC + casefold) before replacing backslashes and normalizing, so fullwidth solidus/reverse solidus are collapsed like their ASCII forms; two new reserved cases (fullwidth separators) in the parametrized test; no over-blocking of nested names (existing not-reserved cases still pass)

test_agent_workspace_service_skill_rows.py asserts an edit writes only to owner workspace-<id>, repoints the row and bumps the version, never writes to the skill owner, and delete only soft-deletes; mutation-checked: letting the edit write to the existing skill owner makes two of the tests fail
